source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ πάντα Χριοτιανὸν ἐγκαταλείπειν μάρτυρας Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἀπιέναι πρὸς τοὺς ψευδομάρτυρας, τουτέστιν αἱρετικῶν, ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους· οὗτοι γὰρ ἀλλότριοι τοῦ Θεοῦ τυγχάνουσιν. Ἔστωσαν οὖν ἀνάθεμα οἱ ἀπερχόμενοι πρὸς αὐτούς.
thought_title: No visiting the false martyrs of heretics
orientation: The council continues forbidding contact with heretics by regulating whose martyrs Christians may visit.
pass_a_gloss: That every Christian must not abandon the martyrs of Christ, and go away to the false martyrs, that is, those of heretics, or themselves having become to the above said heretics; for these happen to be strangers to God. Therefore let those going away to them be accursed.

choices.why: keeps genitive of belonging and contrasts with false martyrs in next clause

choices.english: false martyrs, that is, those of heretics
choices.why: literal gloss of explanatory phrase without importing existing canon wording

choices.english: happen to be strangers to God
choices.why: preserves τυγχάνουσιν force and ἀλλότριος estrangement sense
uses brief glossary English accursed and keeps command wish force

pass_b_english: No Christian should abandon the martyrs of Christ and turn to false martyrs. These are the martyrs of heretics, or those who have themselves joined those same heretics. They are strangers to God. Let anyone who goes to them be accursed.
notes: Χριοτιανὸν is misspelled by transposition for Χριστιανὸν; glossed as Christian
Clause ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους is syntactically unclear; glossed word for word without supplying missing sense

problems.quote: These are the martyrs of heretics, and so is anyone who has joined those same heretics.
problems.source_quote: τουτέστιν αἱρετικῶν, ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους
problems.why: Source says the false martyrs are those of heretics, or of those who have gone over to the aforesaid heretics. English wrongly calls the person a martyr and garbles the grammar.
problems.fix: No Christian should abandon the martyrs of Christ and go to the false martyrs, that is, those of heretics, or of those who have joined the aforementioned heretics.

edits.old: These are the martyrs of heretics, and so is anyone who has joined those same heretics.
edits.new: These are the martyrs of heretics, or of those who have themselves joined those same heretics.

fixed: Real mistranslation: Greek τουτέστιν αἱρετικῶν, ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους describes two classes of false martyrs, not the visiting Christian becoming a martyr; fixed to `or of those who have themselves joined`.

problems.quote: or of those who have themselves joined those same heretics
problems.source_quote: ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους
problems.why: The accusative names people who have themselves gone over to the heretics, not martyrs belonging to such people.
problems.fix: These are the false martyrs of heretics, or people who have themselves gone over to those heretics.
problems.ruling: αὐτοὺς ... γενομένους is accusative, parallel to ψευδομάρτυρας: the martyrs themselves joined the heretics. English 'of those who' makes them martyrs belonging to converts, which changes the meaning.

edits.old: These are the martyrs of heretics, or of those who have themselves joined those same heretics.
edits.new: These are the martyrs of heretics, or those who have themselves joined those same heretics.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: removed second 'of' because ἢ αὐτοὺς πρὸς τοὺς προειρημένους αἱρετικοὺς γενομένους is accusative in apposition to ψευδομάρτυρας, naming the false martyrs themselves as people gone over, not martyrs belonging to such people.
